newsitem.title: UK: Maharishi sect selling British country mansion.
newsitem.headline: Maharishi sect selling British country mansion.

text.p: The Maharishi Foundation, which follows the guru who taught The Beatles to meditate, is selling its sumptuous British headquarters for up to 15 million pounds ($25 million), sales agents said on Tuesday.
The Maharishi Foundation is putting Mentmore Towers, one of Britain's most important country houses, on the market because it wants to move to more spacious premises elsewhere in the country.
Sales agents Savills said the house, with five state reception rooms, about 50 bedrooms and extensive grounds, was expected to fetch between 10 and 15 million pounds.

Mentmore Towers, located in central England, was built in 1855 for Baron Meyer Amschel de Rothschild of the famous banking family and became the home of the Earl of Rosebery, prime minister from 1894-95.

The house hit the headlines in 1977 when its entire contents, one of the finest private collections of art and antiques, was auctioned for six million pounds in what became known as "the sale of the century".
The Maharishi Foundation bought Mentmore Towers in 1978 for about 250,000 pounds.
The foundation is guided by the Maharishi Mahesh Yogi, who taught The Beatles the art of transcendental meditation in the 1960s.

Foundation chairman Geoffrey Clements said: "Mentmore has been a superb home for the foundation, ideal both for our everyday needs and to entertain our local and international guests. The success we are experiencing with our activities means we are looking for a new home."
